items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: there wasn't no string bass out here but me and Montuti.

ctx.x: Oh, I heard of him, too.

Yeah. See? Did he pick the bass? He was picking, picking, picking, wasn't slapping, just picking. Picking it. Oh, yes. See? So, so, they can't, they can't give those, those guys credit. But when I come, when I went around New York, when I left Los Angeles, even in L.A., in 22, there wasn't no string bass out here but me and Montuti. See, nobody didn't pay no attention to Montuti. Didn't start to pay attention to Montuti until I come out here with the Ory band. After I went, Ory went with the black and tan band,…

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: We'd fix him, guy -- Pops can tell you.

ctx.x: We'd fix him, guy -- Pops can tell you. I jump -- a guy jump up there and want to play, you understand, look over at him and Pops (unintelligible), just stomp, you know, bam-bam-, you know. He say what key? He says, follow. Just follow, and you know what we said, take him around the belt means --

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Is he older than you at Garland?

ctx.x: How many strings did you have? Three. Three strings.
All the bass players, Eddie Corbidora band, but I was playing three string bass. I'm one of the rips. Is he older than you at Garland? Yeah. He's older than you. Yeah. He's up in the 70s.
He gave a seven one order, he's way up in the 70s, two. I didn't want to say 70.
